name: Jo Bloom
life: “I still remember calling a halt from the back of a van.” People around Breakwater Way know Jo by a small Thursday habit. Jo stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I thought it was a safety warning and stopped a delivery. I'm glad I did.
appearance: Jo has short copper curls, fine brows over wide-set eyes, and a favorite piece of clothing, an olive canvas jacket. It usually goes with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case. When somebody else has the floor, Jo counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Jo has excellent recall for voices and a poor memory for official titles. Someone who waited patiently at a counter years ago is more likely to be remembered than the person in charge.
agenda: To reopen the platform after the wording is understood.
family: Joseph Moran is Jo’s older cousin. Jo calls about good news first. Joseph is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *The gift nobody wants*, Joseph says, “I made money selling buildings. I thought the finest gift I could give her was never having to ask a landlord for anything.”
connections: Ruth Tran. The shift stopped for a warning gives a carpenter time to save the marked board.

reactions.situation: A contractor wants to scrub the chalk under the quay
reactions.response: Jo takes a photograph and asks whose permission is needed before the chalk is touched.

reactions.situation: A neighbor offers to pay for a favor that was meant kindly
reactions.response: Jo accepts a small agreed amount if paying lets the neighbor keep their pride.
